chapter: Hippolyte Charles, the bass and other bands
title: Playing Scotch, French and German tunes; leading Joe Oliver's band on mandolin
summary: Dawson talks about violin repertoire and quadrilles and cakewalks, and says he once led a seven-piece Joe Oliver band on mandolin at a lake picnic.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players

blocks.x: And what about uh... Well, Pete Boccage used to play some of those funny little instruments. No, violin. The only violin when you do it? That's all I know. What kind of music did you play on the violin? What type of music?

The classic music. Pete, like when Pete taught... Not what about the mandolin? Oh, we'd play anything. Yeah. I could play a selection of Scotch, uh... French... Yeah. And uh... German music. I could... I'd play any kind of number like that, but I know, you know, they like the people... We playing for... I was good on it, yeah. Do you remember any of the names of any of these numbers? No, just Head. You played by Head you didn't? No, no music, no.
What about cakewalks? Did you ever play any cakewalks? I played quadrille, cakewalks.

Yeah. Yeah. You know, I'll tell you the truth. You might take... But I don't know if it's ever in the party. No, it's all day, all gone. But I played a picnic at the lake with a mandolin, with a band, a whole band, with Joe Oliver's band. They didn't have no violin, they didn't put me on the mandolin. I was leading, I was leading the band with mandolin. I knew all them numbers. Yeah. That's the truth. You never heard of them. You had a seven-piece band, and I was leading with a mandolin.
